main_issue: Whether the housewarming should serve alcohol (A's bought drinks) given D's religious objection, or whether a compromise such as a cooler box or landing placement is acceptable.

A-B.evidence: B proposes cooler box/landing compromises (8, 23) and rebukes A ('We're all hosts', 15); A dismisses D's hosting role (14) and ends with 'no compromise' (26). A never takes up B's ideas.

A-C.evidence: C backs cooler (9) and landing (24) and wants it resolved before Saturday (18); A keeps insisting on the party with drinks and rejects D (26), without adopting C's compromises.

A-D.evidence: D rejects alcohol at the party (11, 13, 25); A says 'So don't be a host' (14) and 'either your way, or nothing' (26). D offers to pay A back (21) and A refuses (22).

B-C.evidence: C endorses B's cooler idea (9), supports B's concern about the manager (18), and backs the landing idea (24).

B-D.evidence: B wants D included as a host (15) and offers compromises; D appreciates them but says they don't solve it (11, 25). Both want a resolution but differ on the arrangement.

C-D.evidence: C backs the cooler box and landing (9, 24); D says these don't change things for her (11, 25). Both want to avoid conflict, but C is more open to alcohol being present.
